changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 2 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6238-object-payload-enabled.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` — edited by this change

  > **No published type changed.** `ObjectMetadataPayload` is exported from its module but that module is not re-exported by `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts`, the package's only entry, so the removed `enabled?: boolean` was never on the published surface and no `**/src/index.ts` is touched. What consumers *can* observe is behaviour: `MetadataService` is reachable through the published `useMetadataService()` hook, both method signatures are unchanged (`PromiseANGLE-BRACKETS(void)`), and the HTTP request they issue changes from a `PUT` with a body to a `DELETE`.

### `.changeset/6559-expression-user-input-contract.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` — edited by this change

  > WHAT BREAKS, AND FOR WHOM. This tightens a signature published from the package entry (`packages/app-shell/src/index.ts`), so an external caller that passes an unchecked or under-declared value stops compiling on upgrade. That is accepted (maintainer ruling 2026-08-27, option A): the only calls it refuses are calls that were never conformant with the contract the module already declared. It ships as `minor`, not `major` — objectui's major tracks `@objectstack`'s, so its own breaking changes ship as a minor with the break written down (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`). ⛔ Keeping `unknown` and ⛔ adding a second, wider entry point were both declined.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Angle-bracketed names in the quoted prose above are rewritten as `ANGLE-BRACKETS(name)`: GitHub deletes tag-shaped fragments from a stored body, and a quote that silently loses the identifier it is about is worse than a visible repair.

Compared the checked-out tree with `480de81fd` (merge-base with origin/main): 5 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1733 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2337 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36538501139)

## Contract review

Inputs: card #11058 (body, triage ruling `5885257659`, claim `5885596509`, `os-dev-report` `5885956484`), PR #11063 (body, 6-file list, net diff against `main` at `480de81fd`, `+179 / -8`, one commit), and the head's check-runs (`filter=latest`, read after every run completed: 43 runs, 40 `success`, 3 `skipped` — the two coverage lanes and `dependabot` — 0 failures, none pending; the eight test shards, the `Test` aggregate, `Type Check`, `Lint` and `Spec Main Shape Gate` were still in progress when this review began and were waited for). The sign-up twin's two records on PR #11052 (`5884718105` FAIL on the bump level, `5884917329` PASS) were read as context for what that map was already judged on; nothing in them is an input to this head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Public surface widens by one export** — `signInRefusalMessages(t: TranslateFn): Record of string to string`, new module `packages/app-shell/src/console/auth/signInRefusalMessages.ts`, added to the `@object-ui/app-shell` entry (`packages/app-shell/src/index.ts`, the line after `DefaultLoginPage`, mirroring `signUpRefusalMessages` after `DefaultRegisterPage`). **Right.** Triage ruled one sign-in map owned by `@object-ui/app-shell` and passed by both login pages; the console app is a separate package, so the map has to be exported. The parameter is typed with the one `TranslateFn` authority (`packages/i18n/src/translateFn.ts`, re-exported from the `@object-ui/i18n` entry), exactly as the sign-up map is; `useObjectTranslation()`'s `t` satisfies that shape on both pages. The return shape equals `LoginForm`'s prop `errorMessages?: Record of string to string` (`packages/auth/src/LoginForm.tsx`).
2. **`DefaultLoginPage` now passes `errorMessages={signInRefusalMessages(t)}`.** **Right** — this is the card. `LoginForm`'s accept set does not move: its two catches (`handleSubmit` and `handleSendOtp`) still read `(code && errorMessages?.[code]) || authError.message`, untouched, so a code the map does not name still shows the server message.
3. **The console `LoginPage` drops its inline map and passes the same call.** **Right** — the ruling's "no second hand-written copy". The set is byte-identical to what was removed: `INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD` on `auth.login.errors.invalidCredentials`, `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` on `auth.login.errors.emailNotVerified`, with the same two inline `defaultValue` strings, which match the `en` pack verbatim (`en.ts`, the `auth.login.errors` block); `zh` carries distinct translations for both keys. `apps/console` already declares `@object-ui/app-shell: workspace:*` (its `devDependencies`, the same edge the merged twin's `RegisterPage` already imports `signUpRefusalMessages` over), and `App.tsx` / `main.tsx` already import the barrel, so no dependency edge and no eager-closure growth is introduced (`Bundle Analysis`, the job that runs `check-eager-closure-budget.mjs`, is green on the head).
4. **No locale-pack key is added.** **Right** — both keys exist in `zh` and `en` at the head (the dev reports all ten packs; `all-locales-key-parity` runs in the test shards); no `packages/i18n/src/locales/*` file is in the diff, as the claim's "⛔ no pack key added" asked.
5. **The console page's `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` branch stays where it is.** **Right**, and it is the measurement the ruling asked for ("it moves only if it is the same text"). It is not text: `LoginFormCard`'s `onError` navigates to the console-only `/verify-email-prompt` route. And the ruling's premise that it "runs before the map" does not hold in the source: `LoginForm`'s catch calls `setError(mapped)` first and `onError` after it, so the mapped text is set on the console page too and the redirect then replaces the page. The dev recorded the falsified premise in the report and the module's docblock says why the branch stays; the console page's redirect code is untouched by the diff.
6. **Pin** `packages/app-shell/src/console/auth/__tests__/loginRefusalCodes-11058.test.tsx`: the exported page under `zh`, one case per mapped code (2, covering both pack keys), the unknown-code fallback, and a zh-differs-from-en guard; expected text read from the packs; the real form, a real `AuthProvider` over a real `createAuthClient` and a real `I18nProvider`, only `fetch` stubbed at `/sign-in/email`. **Right** and as ruled ("zh per code on the exported page, plus the unknown-code fallback"). It is the sibling of `registerRefusalCodes-11030.test.tsx` in the same collection (same render stack, same `tsconfig.test.json` glob). `Test (shard 1..8/8)`, `Test`, `Test (dist pins)`, `Type Check` and `Lint` are green on the head.
7. **Changeset package set** — `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/console`. **Right**: both are in the `fixed` group of `.changeset/config.json`, `apps/console/src` changed, and `check-changeset-presence.mjs` guards fixed-group `src/**` (`Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Changeset Claim Re-read`, `Changeset Overwrite Report`, `Changeset Bump Policy` all green on the head). The level is judged in ②.
8. **The two pending changesets whose bodies name the app-shell entry** — `6238-object-payload-enabled.md` (`ObjectMetadataPayload` is not re-exported by `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts`) and `6559-expression-user-input-contract.md` (`buildExpressionUser`'s tightened signature) — stay true at the head: this diff adds only the `signInRefusalMessages` re-export and touches neither name. **Right**, read at the head.
9. Nothing else in the diff touches an accept set or a published surface. The six files are exactly the claim's file surface; the barrel edit is the export the claim's own `Why yes` names. The PR's labels (`apps`, `tests`, `package: app-shell`) are the labeler's, not the dev's. `check:i18n-keys` (every inline `defaultValue` equals the pack value) runs in the `Type Check` job on the head, green.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes` on the PR (and on the claim). **Right** — item ①.1 is a purely additive widening of a published package's public surface.
- `.changeset/11058-signin-refusal-map.md` grades `'@object-ui/app-shell': minor`, `'@object-ui/console': patch`. **Right.** A `Clause-②: yes` takes at least `minor` (the fleet's one reader of the line, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`: "`yes` / `yes (widening)` … both take at least `minor`"), which is exactly the level the twin's FAIL record `5884718105` set for `signUpRefusalMessages` and this PR carries from the start. The console entry publishes no widening (the fixed group takes the highest level in any case). The body names the new export and the unchanged fallback and states no bump level, so it does not contradict its own front matter (`Changeset Claim Re-read` green). No `major` anywhere (`Changeset Bump Policy` green).
- Level and declaration match what the diff publishes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **D1 — commit trailer pair (model-free pair, session-URL PR footer) vs the harness reminder:** reported, not re-judged: commit messages are outside this record's inputs; the PR body ends with the session-URL footer objectui's AGENTS.md asks for.
- **D2 — declared narrowings** (`pnpm test` farm, repo-wide `pnpm lint`, `check:eager-closure` NOT MEASURED, `check:readme-exports` NOT MEASURED): all answered by the head's check-runs — `Test (shard 1..8/8)`, `Test`, `Lint`, `Bundle Analysis` (eager-closure budget), `README Export Check`, all green.
- **D3 — a one-shot console control test, written, run at the base and at the head, deleted, never committed:** accepted. No such file is in the 6-file list; the ruled pins are on the exported page and are committed (①.6). Observation, not a condition: unlike the register twin (which had `registerRefusalCodes-10998` on the console page as a committed control), the console login page keeps no committed pin for these two codes — its existing `LoginPage.error-banner` and `LoginPage.dev-admin-hint` pins render the page through the new import but drive no refusal. The console text comes from the same function with byte-identical keys (①.3), so nothing on this head needs it.
- **Premise partly falsified** (triage's "the branch runs before the map"): answered in ①.5 from `LoginForm`'s source; the ruling's own condition ("moves only if it is the same text") decides it, and the branch is a redirect, not text.
- **`open_questions`:** none declared; none found.
- **Out-of-scope finding 1 (phone sign-in refusal codes unmapped; carrier 承接者:无):** real in the source — `LoginForm` feeds the same `errorMessages` to its phone-OTP and phone-password branches and to `handleSendOtp`, and the map names no phone code, so a refused phone sign-in shows the server's message on both login pages. Escalated to the seat: file it as its own card (read-from-source, no pack key exists, dedupe words are in the report) or record on #11058 why not. Not a condition of this PR — the card names the two email codes.
- **Out-of-scope finding 2 (the console redirect also matches on the English message text, not only the code):** an observation on untouched console code; escalated to the seat with the first, same carrier. Not a condition of this PR.
